text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired: LB target_health unhealthy (us-east-1), TLS handshake error rate spiking, DNS lookup latency increased. auto-escalation to oncall.

pagerduty: ALERT: service=redwood-api-lb | severity=high | 503_rate=27% | tls_handshake_fail=18% | affected_region=us-east-1

Elena: acked. I'm on it. jumping to runbook -> https://redwood.runbooks/lb-tls-dns

Ryan: seeing increased 5xx from the edge -> ALB reports multiple targets UNHEALTHY across two subnets. Also some TCP RSTs during TLS handshakes.

Maria: capturing network traces. can you paste recent envoy logs? if we need to failover we'll do a regional weight shift.

Elena: pasting snippet from healthchecks:
```
2026-03-14T16:23:10Z target/10.12.34.5 UNHEALTHY code=503 check="/healthz"
2026-03-14T16:23:12Z target/10.12.34.6 UNHEALTHY code=523 tls_error="handshake_failure"
2026-03-14T16:23:15Z target/10.12.34.7 UNHEALTHY code=503
```

Josh: support intake: multiple customers reporting timeout/errors on inference calls. most reports from east coast customers. collecting affected customer ids now.

SupportBot: Customer impact summary: 48 calls failed in the last 5m, top paths: /v1/generate, /v1/chat/stream. SLA Pages: 2 customers with high impact (realtime chat). Ticket links: https://tickets.redwood/INC-4759

Elena: quick mitigation plan:
- step1: move 30% traffic from us-east-1 -> us-west-2 (weight shift)
- step2: scale up healthy target group in us-east by +2 nodes
- step3: temporarily raise ALB healthcheck timeout from 3s -> 10s to give long cold-start models wiggle room
- step4: if TLS handshake rate doesn't drop in 3m, fallback route to non-mutual-tls variant

Ryan: can do weight shift. running command now:
```
aws elbv2 modify-listener --listener-arn arn:alb:us-east-1:... --default-actions Type=forward,TargetGroupArn=arn:tg:... --weight=70
```

incident-bot: action started by Ryan (weight shift to us-west-2 = 30%). auto-page to infra-oncall if no ack in 2m.

Maria: I see a spike in TLS alerts tied to a cert rotation job that ran ~16:20. Checking cert chain and cipher mismatches.

Elena: rolling back cert rotation on a single host to test. command:
```
ssh ubuntu@10.12.34.6 sudo /opt/redwood/certs/rollback.sh --prev
```

Ryan: weight shift applied. us-east now 70%, us-west 30%. probing endpoints...

Elena: after rollback on 10.12.34.6, handshake failure rate dropped on that host. overall TLS error rate down from 18% -> 7%.

SupportBot: update posted to affected customers draft: "We're experiencing increased errors in us-east-1. We're shifting traffic and mitigating; we will follow up with RCA." Request approval to send.

Josh: approved. send now.

pagerduty: escalation policy: second-level oncall paged (no response from infra team yet). paging Maria.

Maria: I'm on the traces. the root cause looks like a broken cert chain on the rotation job plus a small subset of unhealthy targets failing healthchecks which amplified ALB rebalancing. DNS propagation noise (recent change to alias weights) made retries worse.

Elena: action items we completed:
- weight shift applied -> reduced immediate customer impact
- scaled target group +2 (nodes launching)
- rolled back cert on one host which improved TLS handshake rates
- increased healthcheck timeout as temporary buffer

Elena: next steps:
- continue monitoring for 15m, if steady -> revert healthcheck timeout to 3s and keep weight shift at 70/30 for cooldown window
- full rollback of the cert rotation across the fleet if handshake issues persist
- postmortem and timeline (assign to Maria + Ryan)

Ryan: adding run commands to incident doc and exporting ALB metrics to S3:
```
aws cloudwatch get-metric-statistics --namespace AWS/ELB --metric-name HTTPCode_Target_5XX_Count --start-time 2026-03-14T16:15:00Z --end-time 2026-03-14T16:45:00Z --period 60
```

incident-bot: Incident state -> mitigated (customer error rate decreased by 65%). auto-note: initiated followup task: /postmortem create "LB TLS cert rotation caused regional handshake spike" assigned to @Maria @Ryan due in 3 days.

Elena: handing off to monitoring rotation in 10m. if anything regresses -> re-open page. thanks team.

Maria: will own postmortem. collecting logs and cert job diffs now.

Josh: updating tickets and customer comms. pushing status update to support channels.

SupportBot: final customer update posted. affected customers notified. ticketing updated: link https://tickets.redwood/INC-4759/updates/1

Ryan: marking runbook edits: add a step to validate cert chain post-rotation and include canary healthcheck targets.

Elena: closing this thread; followups tracked in the postmortem and runbook PR. :white_check_mark:
